close_reason: Deleted 13 vacuous inline tests across 8 method files. Kept the 4 tests that legitimately exercise build_request / USING_* constants. description:
Tests in src/methods/calendar.rs:149-176, src/methods/event.rs:212-241, src/methods/event_copy.rs:50-64, src/methods/event_notification.rs:191-241, src/methods/participant_identity.rs:110-138, src/methods/event_parse.rs:60-107, src/methods/principal_availability.rs:73-123, and src/methods/mod.rs:393-423 follow this pattern:

```
let args = json!({...});  // hand-built mock of what the production method WOULD build
let req = build_request("Method/name", args, USING_CALENDARS);
assert_eq!(calls[0][0], json!("Method/name"));
```

These tests prove only that `build_request` echoes its inputs. They do NOT prove that `calendar_get`, `calendar_event_set`, `calendar_event_query`, etc. CALL `build_request` with those exact arguments. If the production method body had a typo ("Calendar/Get" instead of "Calendar/get", or "sinceState" → "since_state"), every one of these tests would still pass.

The pattern that has actual coverage value lives in tests/availability_tests.rs:60-86: it inspects `server.received_requests()` after calling the production method. Apply that pattern to the wire-shape tests too, OR remove these vacuous tests; they currently lock in the wrong invariant.
